source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check version of BMC/BIOS from BIOS
2. Send command to check version of BMC : ipmitool raw 0x30 0x20

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Command should be sent successfully
2. Versions should be shown correctly before and after flashing.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X GET https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory | jq .FirmwareInventory[]|select(.Name|test("RoT|Root of Trust"))
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the FirmwareInventory entry matching RoT. No RISK.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; broad name matching neither identifies the active Root of Trust nor proves its firmware version, and it weakens TLS/secret handling.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / IMPROVED; correctly separates version evidence from attestation, but assumes a supplied mapping may replace the contradictory Master operation without an engineering decision.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 741/2291 accepts the name-regex collection and leaves the RoT versus BMC/BIOS mismatch unresolved.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its FULLY AUTOMATABLE result is non-counting history; it treats the source-design conflict and security scope as ordinary readiness inputs.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves source, ED-36 permits BLOCKED for unresolved target/core-operation semantics, ED-38 reserves final verdicts and ED-39 requires exact firmware-target identity.

original_test_intent: The Items request the active platform Root-of-Trust firmware version before and after a separate approved update; they do not state that version equality alone validates the trust chain or attestation.
original_method: The preserved Procedure checks BMC/BIOS and sends BMC raw `0x30 0x20`. DeepSeek replaces that with a generic Redfish name regex, without identifying the active RoT or canonical version property.
manual_activity: The platform/security owner must resolve whether this source is a RoT version-only test or the copied BMC/BIOS check, identify the active trust component and state whether attestation is separately required before collection is meaningful.
required_inputs: engineering decision on RoT versus BMC/BIOS purpose
security-owner identification of the active RoT component/resource
canonical version property and expected before/after release pair
trusted authenticated inventory channel and evidence rules
safety_requirements: Use no RoT provisioning, key enrollment, firmware update, reset, security-setting change or undocumented raw command in this version review.
Do not infer active trust-anchor identity, authenticity or attestation from a matching name or version string.
Reject `curl -k` and logged basic credentials; require verified TLS and approved secret injection.
Preserve complete inventory and any separately approved measurement/signature artifacts with exact component binding.
Stop on ambiguity or mismatch; do not retry automatically or attempt remediation.
agent_execution_scope: No execution while the target and security scope remain unresolved.
After approval, collect the exact active RoT version property read-only and compare it to the release matrix; collect attestation only when separately specified.
Report facts and security discrepancies without assigning the DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve whether RoT is the authoritative target and whether this testcase is version-only or also covers attestation.
Approve the active component mapping, canonical property, expected values and any Project Override coverage.
Review complete evidence and issue the final PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The command assumes a collection shape, disables certificate validation and may return similarly named inactive/security components; a name match is neither a version comparison nor trust validation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until engineering/security ownership resolves target and scope. Then use trusted discovery and exact active-component binding, with version and attestation evidence kept distinct.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RoT Items, copied BMC/BIOS procedure, raw `0x30 0x20`, Criteria, script and 5/0-minute values remain unchanged source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the active RoT hardware/function to a documented read-only inventory/version property, compare before/after values with the approved release, and add measurement/signature/attestation checks only as a separately approved checkpoint.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the platform and active RoT design approved by security ownership.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record RoT, BMC, Redfish schema, client and attestation-tool revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform RoT architecture, vendor firmware inventory and security/attestation specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing RoT-specific read and scope separation as a recommendation without rewriting the BMC/BIOS Master source.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Version equality cannot prove authenticity, active-root selection or trust-chain validity; those need distinct evidence when in scope.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target decision, active component mapping, expected release and security scope.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Misidentifying an inactive RoT-like component can falsely qualify a security baseline.

project_override_considerations: After target/scope approval, Project SPEC may select Redfish, SPDM, attestation or vendor tools, but must bind evidence to the same active RoT and record whether coverage is version-only or includes trust validation. It may not claim attestation from inventory strings.
expected_evidence: engineer/security-owner approved purpose, scope and active RoT identity
complete trusted discovery and exact component/member response
canonical version comparison against the approved before/after release
separate measurement/signature/attestation evidence only when explicitly required
security/BMC/host health, audit timestamps and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items require RoT version, while the Master Procedure is explicitly BMC/BIOS and has no RoT identity, version property or security scope. The generic Criteria cannot determine what component or assurance level must pass.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is a target/core-operation and security-scope contradiction, not merely missing credentials or an expected value. Engineering and security ownership must authorize the intended RoT operation and scope before a valid test can be executed.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to BLOCKED because a broad insecure name query cannot identify or validate the active RoT.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps its component and attestation boundaries but changes confirmation-gated to BLOCKED until the source purpose and security scope are resolved.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because automation cannot choose the active trust component or authorize whether attestation is part of acceptance.

review_improvement: Prevents firmware inventory naming from being reported as Root-of-Trust validation and makes the version-versus-attestation boundary explicit.
independent_technical_reasoning: RoT version readback can eventually be automated, but the source defines no RoT operation and instead checks BMC/BIOS. DeepSeek's regex cannot prove active component identity, and even a correct version does not establish trust state. These unresolved semantics require engineering/security ownership, so the record is BLOCKED at execution readiness while preserving the original source and making no DUT claim.
